To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
asphyxia is a very complex process, which is not only a result of the duration of the asphyxia, but also of other factors.
the duration of asphxia suffices to cause molecular changes in the lungs, but these molecular changes are not detectable in a macroscopical and histological form.
The duration of asphyxial episode (max. 30 min) is not sufficient to trigger a significant increase of alveolar inflammatory cells in the lung.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new aspect in the diagnosis of asphixia death.
the evaluation of the lung tissue reaction pattern as a response to the asphyxia process.
the search for new markers of asphyxia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lung is not a specific organ for the diagnosis of suffocation.
the time of suffocation is not sufficient to cause any significant changes in the lung.
the time of the asphyxia episode does not suffice to trigger a specific reaction pattern of the lung.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the duration of asphixia is not sufficient to cause any significant histological or immunohistochemical changes.
the lung tissue is a very sensitive indicator of hypoxic conditions, but not a specific one.
the duration of the asphyxia process is not long enough to induce a significant change of lung tissue cells, which would be visible in a histological section.

, despite the lack of specificity, the macroscopical findings are of paramount importance in the evaluation of suffocation.
